digest_args.user_message: What does the term 'idempotent' actually mean, and how does it relate to the retry logic we already have?
digest_args.plan_goal: Explain idempotency and connect it to the retry policy
digest_args.plan_rationale: the concept plus the existing policy card answer it
digest_args.draft_answer: An operation is idempotent when running it twice leaves the system in the same state as running it once, so a duplicate delivery is harmless. That is exactly what makes your retry policy safe: it retries on timeout, and a timeout cannot tell a lost request from a slow one, so the retry may duplicate a call that already succeeded. I can map which endpoints are not yet idempotent if that would help.
